full_text:
Russian attack on Odesa facility kills three, injures three more
Meanwhile, 
a Russian ⁠attack ⁠on ​an infrastructure facility ⁠in Ukraine’s ⁠southern ​city ‌of ‌Odesa on Monday ‌killed at least three ‌people and injured ​three others,
 ⁠a city official ​said, as reported by Reuters.
Key events
Italy condemns Russia's move to expel military attache from Moscow 'without cause'
Meanwhile, 
Italy’s foreign minister Antonio Tajani said that 
Russia
 had expelled an Italian military attache and one of his aides from Moscow “without cause,” AFP reported.
Tajani 
wrote on X
 that it represented 
a “blatant act of retaliation for Italy’s expulsion of two Russian military attachés”
, whom he said had been caught spying against Rome.
Deputy prime minister Antonio Tajani during the bilateral summit between prime minister Meloni and Portuguese prime minister Montenegro at Palazzo Chigi, Rome.
 Photograph: Francesca Bolla/AGF/Shutterstock
Hungary opens probe into Chinese BYD carmaker's investment in country negotiated by previous government
Separately, 
Hungary’s government announced an investigation Monday into a large foreign investment by Chinese automaker BYD negotiated by a former foreign minister who last week resigned from parliament to take an executive position at the company,
 AP reported.
Péter Szijjártó’s
 announcement last Wednesday that he would take the job at the world’s top electric carmaker prompted accusations of a conflict of interest and criticism over his role in facilitating substantial government subsidies to the company while in office.
Prime minister 
Péter Magyar
 told lawmakers on Monday that Szijjártó, a close ally of former prime minister 
Viktor Orbán,
 had helped BYD while he was in office “with hundreds of billions (of forints) in public money, diplomatic support and state infrastructure.”
“
We will examine all the decisions,
 negotiations and state commitments made by Péter Szijjártó that were related to the BYD Hungary investment,” Magyar said..
He added the investigation would look into all subsidies, tax breaks, permits, environmental exemptions and publicly funded investments given to large multinational firms during Orbán’s tenure, AP said.
Chinese electric and hybrid car manufacturer, is building a factory near Szeged, Hungary
 Photograph: Zsuzsa Darab/The Guardian
Hungary’s Magyar picks chess prodigy for president after ousting Orbán-era loyalist
European community affairs correspondent 
In other news, 
Hungary’s prime minister, Péter Magyar, has announced plans to ask Judit Polgár, widely considered the greatest female chess player of all time, to take on the largely ceremonial role of president.
Judit Polgár at The Variety Studio during the 2026 Sundance film festival in Utah.
 Photograph: Variety/Getty Images
Magyar said 
he would meet Polgár on Monday to discuss the matter.
 “Our country needs unity, peace and a president that all Hungarians can be proud of,” he wrote on social media. “Judit Polgár’s name has been synonymous with talent and perseverance for decades.”
The announcement by Magyar 
follows a 
months-long standoff
 between the newly elected leader and Tamás Sulyok,
 the president appointed during former leader Viktor Orbán’s time in power.
Since his 
landslide victory
 in April, 
Magyar has repeatedly called on Sulyok to step down, accusing him of being an Orbán “puppet”
 who had failed to stand up for the country as Orbán’s rightwing, nationalist Fidesz party was criticised for weakening democratic institutions and undermining the rule of law.
Last week Hungary’s parliament – where Magyar’s Tisza party holds a two-thirds majority – voted to back a constitutional amendment that included an 
immediate end to Sulyok’s term.
Russian attack on Odesa facility kills three, injures three more
Meanwhile, 
a Russian ⁠attack ⁠on ​an infrastructure facility ⁠in Ukraine’s ⁠southern ​city ‌of ‌Odesa on Monday ‌killed at least three ‌people and injured ​three others,
 ⁠a city official ​said, as reported by Reuters.
Ukraine's top military leadership denies reports suggesting army chief's sacking
in Kyiv
Ukraine’s top military leadership has denied reports that the country’s commander in chief Col Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi is to be sacked.
In a Facebook post
 published in the last few minutes
 it said claims “circulating in the media, particularly on social media and in certain news outlets are untrue”.
It added:

“Gen 
Oleksandr Syrskyi
 continues to carry out his duties as Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.The Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, Lt Gen 
Andriy Hnatov, also continues to carry out his duties.

Dismissal from these posts takes place on the basis of a decree by the President of Ukraine.”

Zelenskyy’s presidential adviser 
Dmytro Lytvyn
 appeared to confirm the denial.
“Don’t expect any personnel appointments today,” he said, urging people to treat information circulated by the media with caution.
Share
Updated at 
09.13 EDT
Zelenskyy congratulates UK's new prime minister Burnham on his appointment
Meanwhile, Ukraine’s 
Volodymyr Zelenskyy
 is the latest leader to congratulate 
Andy Burnham
 on his appointment as the new British prime minister.
In a post on X, he 
said:

“
Congratulations to Andy Burnham
 @andyburnham on taking office as prime minister of the United Kingdom. We wish the prime minister and the British people every success in addressing the challenges of today.

Britain has always been one of the global leaders. We are ready to work together in all possible formats.
 We highly appreciate the UK’s political, defense, and values-based support. The foundation of our bilateral relationship is stronger than ever, and we will continue to make each other stronger. I’m looking forward to our conversation later today. Thank you!”

Pressure on Ukraine's army chief Syrskyi grows after days of street protests
in Kyiv
Meanwhile, 
Ukrainian media are reporting that Ukraine’s Commander in Chief, Col Gen Oleksandr Syrskyi is to be sacked,
 following five days of noisy street protests calling for his dismissal.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy
 has reportedly agreed to fire Syrskyi after controversially sacking defence minister 
Mykhailo Federov
 last week.
Thousands of demonstrators gathered outside Zelenskyy’s office, calling for Federov’s reinstatement and for the commander in chief’s removal.
Why Ukrainians are protesting against Zelenskyy's dismissal of defence minister – video
The news has not been confirmed, but sources indicate an announcement is expected this afternoon.
 There is speculation 
Federov will be brought back into government
 as deputy prime minister for military industry.
Former Ukrainian defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov summarizes his work in office during a press conference in Kyiv, Ukraine.
 Photograph: Global Images Ukraine/Getty Images
Federov is widely credited with improving Ukraine’s position on the battlefield during his six months in the job. He accused Syrskyi of using Soviet era tactics and allocating resources to brigades based on their “loyalty” rather than data.
“
This sort of culture needs to be eradicated,
 because otherwise we won’t be able to defeat an enemy whose system is plagued by the very same issues,” he said. “We have no other choice if we want to defeat 
Russia
 asymmetrically, with minimal losses.”
Share
Updated at 
08.43 EDT
'No change' in Britain's support for Ukraine, new PM Burnham says as he takes office
Just picking up one more thing from the UK, 
the country’s new prime minister Andy Burnham has pledged to make his first calls to US president Donald Trump and Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
The new British prime minister and leader of the Labour Party, Andy Burnham, speaks to the media as he arrives at 10 Downing Street.
 Photograph: Carl Court/Getty Images
In a clip recorded before he was ⁠officially appointed as British leader but released ​after his ‌speech in Downing ‌Street, Burnham was asked who he would ‌contact first and whether that would be Trump, Zelenskyy or another world leader, Reuters reported.
He replied by saying said those two would be among his ‌first calls.
He said 
he would make clear to Zelenskyy that there would ​be “no change” in Britain’s backing for Ukraine
 and that he would support the Ukrainian leader “100%” as his predecessor ⁠
Keir Starmer
 had done.
“President Zelenskyy will be ​left ​in no doubt whatsoever that 
​Britain’s support is steadfast, ​it is ‌resolute.
 It ​will ​be there for him, and I will be there for him personally too,” Burnham told reporters.
AliExpress fined record €550m by EU for failing to stop sale of illegal and fake goods
In other news, 
the Chinese online retail platform AliExpress has been fined a record €550m (£470m) by the EU over its failure to stop illegal goods including harmful clothing, cosmetics and kitchen gadgets being sold through its site.
AliExpress is the largest online retail operator in the EU with 193 million users.
 Photograph: Sheldon Cooper/SOPA Images/Shutterstock
The European Commission fine is 
the biggest imposed by the bloc under the Digital Services Act (DSA),
 legislation that came into force in 2024 to protect consumers from illegal goods, deceptive or addictive marketing techniques.
Henna Virkkunen, the commission’s executive vice-president for tech sovereignty, security and democracy, said:

“The spread of counterfeit clothing, unsafe toys, dangerous cosmetics and other illegal and harmful products is not an unavoidable cost of shopping online – it is a failure by AliExpress to comply with its obligations under the Digital Services Act.

Scale is not an excuse; risks must be identified and addressed systematically to ensure consumers can safely shop online. Today, we are holding AliExpress to this standard and request it to take action.”

Russian anti-war politician ends run for parliament, citing legal setbacks
Back to 
Russia
 and 
Ukraine, 
Boris Nadezhdin, a Russian anti-war politician who had hoped to ⁠stand in parliamentary elections later this year, has announced he is ending his role ⁠in opposition politics for ⁠now,
 ​blaming what he said were politically-motivated legal setbacks, Reuters reported.
Russian opposition politician Boris Nadezhdin, charged with "demonstrating extremist symbols" for a 2023 video he shared that briefly showed a picture of late opposition leader Alexei Navalny - who died in prison in 2024, talks to the media outside a court building in the town of Dolgoprudny in the Moscow region last week.
 Photograph: Alexander Nemenov/AFP/Getty Images
Nadezhdin, 63, a former liberal lawmaker, 
⁠has been an outspoken critic of Moscow’s war in Ukraine
 but – like some other opposition politicians – had ⁠tried to work within the rules of Russia’s tightly controlled ​political system to be ‌able to continue to ‌voice his views publicly.
In a statement, 
Nadezhdin said ‌he had ran out of political road however, after a series of setbacks. He received a small fine on Friday for displaying “extremist symbols” and was this month designated a “foreign agent” by the justice ministry.
Both rulings ‌disqualified him from running for the State Duma, the lower house of parliament, in September ​elections, his statement said. He said he had also been banned from leaving Russia.
Starmer formally resigns as British prime minister, with Burnham set to be confirmed as his successor
Over in the UK, Keir Starmer has now left 10 Downing Street for the last time and resigned as the UK’s prime minister,
 and we are waiting for 
Andy Burnham
 to be formally named as his successor.
Outgoing British prime minister Keir Starmer (C-R) delivers a farewell speech outside 10 Downing Street.
 Photograph: Andy Rain/EPA
British prime minister Keir Starmer greets members of the media as he and his wife, Victoria Starmer, walk to their car, after Starmer delivered his final statement outside 10 Downing Street.
 Photograph: Temilade Adelaja/Reuters
You can follow all of that on our UK live blog with 
Andrew Sparrow:
The European Commission has been asked to respond to mass protests against Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s decision to fire a popular defence minister last week (
10:41
).
Commission chief spokesperson 
Paula Pinho
 said the issue “came up briefly” in commission president von der Leyen’s recent discussions with Zelenskyy, but declined to comment in any further detail.

“But what we can say is that we have enjoyed good cooperation with minister Fedorov at a crucial moment of the defence and defence policy, both for the EU and for Ukraine, which we fully appreciated.”

The commission also responded to public demonstrations against Fedorov’s resignation, saying that “peaceful demonstrations are a fundamental right in all democratic countries.”
Share
Updated at 
06.45 EDT
EU pledges to continue close work with Ukraine on reforms, drones, energy under new PM
European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen held a courtesy phone call with the new Ukrainian prime minister, Sergii Koretksyi, this morning.
In a post on X, she said:

“Very good phone call with @KoretskyiUA. 
We will continue cooperating closely on reforms that move Ukraine’s EU accession process forward.
 Our Drone Deal will harness the EU’s industrial strength to produce Ukraine’s most innovative defence equipment at speed and scale. We also discussed preparations ahead of winter and critical energy infrastructure. 
You can count on our full support,
 including in your work to improve energy sector’s governance.”

The European Commission just told reporters that they are further working on more disbursement of the EU’s €90bn loan for 
Ukraine.
Norway sees 'largest fire in modern times' destroy over 100 homes
Nordic correspondent
In other news, 
a fire that burnt down an entire neighbourhood in a town near the Norwegian city of Drammen was still smouldering on Monday and authorities said they expect to be fighting the fire for days to come.
Around 
100 houses in Krokstadelva were destroyed over the weekend
 and around 400 people evacuated.
Smoke and flames rise from a huge fire that has spread from terraced houses by the Krokstadelva in Drammen, Norway.
 Photograph: Thomas Fure/EPA
On Sunday, police told local newspaper Drammens Tidende that they believe 
the fire was caused either be accident or spontaneous combustion.
Ståle Fuglaas,
 operations manager for Norway’s south-east police district, said they plan to continue extinguishing the fire for 10 more days.
“This is a long-term operation in the area. That says something about the heat in the area,” Fuglaas told VG.

“There we will assist evacuees with retrieving any items that have not yet been retrieved from the fire area. A plan is being worked on between the municipality and the emergency services when it comes to returning to safe places.”

Fire services said they have preventively placed water sprinklers in the area and are patrolling with fire crews, drones and helicopters.
“But 
I wouldn’t say we have control, I wouldn’t use that word yet.
 It looks better now than before,” firefighter Erik Smidsrød told VG.
The area affected by a major fire in Drammen, Norway.
 Photograph: SPA/dana press/Shutterstock

Article 5 / A Member of the United Nations against which preventive or enforcement action has been taken by the Security Council may be suspended from the exercise of the rights and privileges of mem- bership by the General Assembly upon the recom- mendation of the Security Council.

Article 6 A Member of the United Nations which has persistently violated the Principles contained in the present Charter may be expelled from the Organization by the General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council.

Accordingly, our respective Governments, through representatives assembled in the city of San Francisco, who have exhibited their full powers found to be in good and due form, have agreed to the present Charter of the United Nations and do hereby establish an international organization to be known as the United Nations.

related.excerpt: Tehran, Iran – Iran has said it has been approached via mediators to end a new bout of fighting with the United States. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said on Monday that Tehran has received “proposals” to end renewed fighting between Iran and the US. But he did not disclose details of the new offer or whether they involved a 10-day truce, as reported by US media. Recommended Stories list of 4 items end of list “Proposals have been raised through mediators and have been passed over to us,” he told reporters during a press conference in Tehran. Baghaei said that diplomatic efforts are coming in lockstep with those of armed forces after recent political divisions between hardliners and more moderate factions. He also urged regional countries not to allow the US military to use their territory to launch or facilitate attacks on Iranian soil in continuation of the US-Israel war on Iran that began on February 28.
